prov.text: Provision for Credit Losses. Provision for credit losses was $1.86 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $62,000 the three months ended September 30, 2025. The provision for credit losses for the three months ended September 30, 2026, included the provision for credit losses on loans of $1.88 million and a recapture of the provision for unfunded commitments of $20,000. The higher provision for 2026 was largely due to loan growth and does not reflect any meaningful borrower specific deterioration.

nonint.text: Noninterest Expense. Noninterest expense was $19.38 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $18.39 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $993,000, or 5.4%. The driver of the increase was salaries and employee benefits, which increased $650,000. The largest component of this increase period over period was health insurance expense, which increased $544,000.

nonop.text: The following tables present the dollar amount of changes in interest income and interest expense for major components of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities. For each category of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, information is provided on changes attributable to: (1) changes in volume multiplied by the old rate; (2) changes in rate, which are changes in rate multiplied by the old volume; and (3) changes not solely attributable to rate or volume, which have been allocated proportionately to the change due to volume and the change due to rate.

tax.text: Provision for Income Taxes. Provision for income taxes was $831,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.33 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The effective tax rate was 21.6% for the current period compared to 26.8% for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

net.text: Net Income. Eagle’s net income for the three months ended September 30, 2026, was $3.01 million, compared to $3.63 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease of $616,000 was due to an increase in noninterest expenses of $993,000 and a decrease in net interest income after provision for credit losses of $498,000. These changes were partially offset by decrease in the provision for income taxes of $495,000 and an increase in noninterest income of $380,000. For the current period, basic earnings per common share and diluted earnings per common share were both $0.38. Basic and diluted earnings per common share were $0.47 and $0.46 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, respectively.

Net interest income.heading: Analysis of Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
The Bank’s earnings have historically depended primarily upon net interest income, which is the difference between interest income earned on loans and investments and interest paid on deposits and any borrowed funds. It is the single largest component of Eagle’s operating income. Net interest income is affected by (i) the difference between rates of interest earned on loans and investments and rates paid on interest-bearing deposits and borrowings (the “interest rate spread”) and (ii) the relative amounts of loans and investments and interest-bearing deposits and borrowings.

The following table includes average balances for financial condition items, as well as interest and dividends and average yields related to the average balances. All average balances are daily average balances. Nonaccrual loans were included in the computation of average balances and reported in loans receivable as loans carrying a zero yield. The yields include the effect of deferred fees and discounts and premiums that are amortized or accreted to interest income or expense.

Noninterest income.text: Noninterest Income. Total noninterest income was $5.10 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $4.72 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $380,000, or 8.1%. This increase was primarily due to an increase of $339,000 in other noninterest income.

intro.text: Eagle Bancorp Montana, Inc. is a bank holding company headquartered in Helena, Montana, and is the holding company of Opportunity Bank of Montana, a community bank established in 1922 that serves consumers and small businesses in Montana through 30 banking offices. Additional information is available on the Bank’s website at www.opportunitybank.com. The shares of Eagle Bancorp Montana, Inc. are traded on the NASDAQ Global Market under the symbol “EBMT.”

lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt (incl. current portion)
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans, current maturities included: financial.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
